summary: The English of 1:7-1:12 is faithful and follows Bartenura and Rambam throughout; only one English change, a word-order improvement in 1:8. The main faults are in the word analysis: many tokens were tied to the wrong homograph in BDB (place names Ain, Azem and Hobah, the god Baal, Shem, 'menstruation' for 'witness', 'foundation' for 'drink', 'father' for 'coming', the verb 'shine' for Hillel), and these are repointed to the Jastrow entries in the pack, or the sense is removed where the pack has no right entry. Other faults: a wrong transmission chain in a 1:8 phrase note, הִזָּהֲרוּ called Hitpael (it is Nifal) in both translation and morphology, the anticipatory suffix in מִתַּלְמִידָיו shown as a construct, wrong grammar notes on 1:11, and two inexact commentary summaries (Rambam 1:7, Bartenura 1:8:2). Morphology patches cover gender and number in עֵינֶיךָ, the Nifal participle label, and two roots.

patches.value: Rambam: do not join the wicked in any kind of love or fellowship, so that you do not learn from his deeds. And when you sin, or see a sinner, do not feel secure and say that God will punish him only in the world to come; do not despair of swift punishment for that sin.
patches.reason: The summary left out that Rambam applies the clause to one's own sin ('כשתחטא') as well as to a sinner one sees, and misread 'במין אחד ממיני האהבה' as describing the prohibition rather than its scope.

patches.value: Judah son of Tabbai and Shimon son of Shetach received from them. Judah son of Tabbai says: Do not make yourself like those who arrange the pleas before the judges. When litigants stand before you, let them be in your eyes like the wicked; and when they depart from before you, let them be in your eyes like the innocent, once they have accepted the judgment upon themselves.
patches.reason: 'accepted upon themselves the judgment' keeps Hebrew word order at the cost of the English; same sense.

value: הִזָּהֲרוּ is a Nifal imperative plural: the נ of the Nifal is assimilated into the doubled ז.
After שֶׁמָּא 'lest' a chain of consequences follows: תָחוּבוּ, then four verbs joined by וְ (וְתִגְלוּ, וְיִשְׁתּוּ, וְיָמוּתוּ, וְנִמְצָא), and last the participle מִתְחַלֵּל.
תָחוּבוּ חוֹבַת is a cognate object, verb and noun from the root חוב ('incur a liability'); גָּלוּת וְתִגְלוּ then repeats the root גלה.
נִמְצָא plus participle: 'it turns out that (the name of Heaven) is being profaned'.
מַיִם הָרָעִים: figurative: the evil waters are heretical teachings that the disciples would 'drink'.
patches.reason: Two notes were wrong: not 'six verbs with וְ' (תָחוּבוּ follows שֶׁמָּא directly and מִתְחַלֵּל is a participle without וְ), and the play on the root is תָחוּבוּ חוֹבַת and גָּלוּת וְתִגְלוּ, not within חוֹבַת גָּלוּת. A note on the Nifal is added.

patches.value: Bartenura: even if there are no heretics where you are, sin may bring exile to a place of people who interpret the Torah against the halakhah ('מראים פנים בתורה שלא כהלכה'); they are the 'evil waters'. They will draw improper meanings from your words, and the disciples who come after you will drink these heretical words and die in their guilt.
patches.reason: 'give the Torah a false appearance' does not render the idiom 'show faces in the Torah not according to the halakhah', which means to interpret it falsely; the step 'they will draw improper meanings from your words' was left out.
הִזָּהֲרוּ is Nifal (assimilated נ doubles the ז: הִזָּהֵר); the Hitpael of זהר would be הִזְדַּהֲרוּ.
שמם is the root 'be desolate'; Jastrow derives שֵׁם 'name' from שׁוּם (jastrow:שֵׁם II: 'v. שׁוּם').

patches.value: מִן + תַּלְמִידָיו 'his disciples': the suffix ־ָיו anticipates שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן ('his disciples, of Aaron' = 'the disciples of Aaron'); מִן is partitive, 'one of'.
patches.reason: The note did not explain the anticipatory suffix, and the literal had it as a construct.

value: הֱוֵי מִתַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן: מִ is partitive, 'one of'. תַּלְמִידָיו 'his disciples' carries a suffix that anticipates the possessor named by שֶׁל: 'his disciples, of Aaron', a common Mishnaic construction.
Four participles, אוֹהֵב, רוֹדֵף, אוֹהֵב, מְקָרְבָן, follow the imperative as a list of Aaron's qualities.
שָׁלוֹם is repeated: 'love peace and pursue peace': a pair of verbs of increasing effort.
הַבְּרִיּוֹת is 'creatures': here human beings generally, not only Israel; מְקָרְבָן has the feminine suffix -ן on 'them'.
patches.reason: The first note did not explain the anticipatory suffix on תַּלְמִידָיו, the point a learner needs here.
